title: Bootstrap-processor migration
blurb: Compares the legacy dummy AudioWorkletNode('bootstrap') workaround side by side with audioWorklet.port, and probes pre-addModule posting, per-context isolation, close(), and transferring WebAssembly bytes vs a compiled WebAssembly.Module.
question: How does migrating off a dummy bootstrap AudioWorkletProcessor behave across config delivery, pre-addModule messages, context isolation, close(), and WebAssembly delivery?
result: On Chrome for Testing 153, the legacy bootstrap node delivered the 4-key config, transferred WebAssembly bytes compiled inside AudioWorkletGlobalScope and returned 21 (3x7), while posting a compiled WebAssembly.Module fired messageerror on a non-cross-origin-isolated page; the shared-port column reported unavailable. Spec path not verified in Chrome 160.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153 (legacy bootstrap and WebAssembly probes verified); not verified in Chrome 160

friction.summary: Posting a compiled WebAssembly.Module to an AudioWorklet MessagePort fires messageerror when the page is not cross-origin isolated
friction.repro: Compile a WebAssembly.Module on the main thread on a non-cross-origin-isolated page and postMessage() it to the worklet port; onmessageerror fires in AudioWorkletGlobalScope.
friction.browser: Chrome for Testing 153 (observed on bootstrap port)
friction.workaround: Transfer the raw ArrayBuffer bytes ([bytes]) over the port and compile with new WebAssembly.Module(bytes) inside AudioWorkletGlobalScope.

friction.summary: Browsers without AudioWorklet.prototype.port require instantiating a dummy AudioWorkletNode solely to borrow a MessagePort to global scope
friction.repro: Check 'port' in AudioWorklet.prototype on Chrome <= 159 or Safari; it is false, forcing a no-op processor whose process() returns false.
friction.browser: Chrome <= 159, Safari (WebKit standards-positions #739 has no signal)
friction.workaround: Keep a single feature-detected helper returning ctx.audioWorklet.port when 'port' in AudioWorklet.prototype is true and falling back to new AudioWorkletNode(ctx, 'bootstrap').port.
